name: Benjamin Netanyahu
role: Prime Minister of Israel (1996-1999, 2009-2021, 2022-present); finance minister (2003-2005)
summary: Likud leader whose record combines free-market economics, a hawkish security and foreign policy centred on Iran and Israeli military strength, and the view that Israel is the nation-state of the Jewish people. He has accepted a demilitarized Palestinian state only under strict conditions and opposes an imposed one, and has championed limiting judicial review. Many of his positions on social, ecological and governance questions are not clearly recorded.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As finance minister (2003-05) he pursued privatization, a smaller public sector and tax cuts, and is widely described as a free-market advocate.

public-ownership.rationale: Privatized banks, El Al and Zim and proposed restructuring ports and the electric company as finance minister.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Cut the top personal rate from 64% to 44% and the corporate rate from 36% to 18%.

unions-good.rationale: Confronted the Histadrut over strikes in 2003 and the Finance Ministry threatened legislation to restrict public-sector strikes.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Repeatedly argued overregulation and bureaucratic barriers choke companies (book, 'Don't Read the Press'); also did impose concentration limits, answered under cartels.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cut welfare payments and introduced welfare-to-work as finance minister; in 2011 chose social-program cuts over defense cuts.

surveillance-ok.rationale: In Fighting Terrorism (1995) he accepts expanded security powers during sustained attacks, with periodic review and judicial oversight.

legalize-drugs.rationale: His cannabis steps were medical expansion and export; he only said he was considering recreational legalization.

strong-leader.rationale: Cast the deciding vote for direct election of the prime minister, to free him from no-confidence votes that interest groups could use to block reform (book, 'Politics 1988-1993').

state-harmful.rationale: Treats a strong state as essential: describes the Jewish state as a haven and makes state power and security the centre of his career (book, 'Nobody Likes Goliath').

empower-police-military.rationale: Raised the defense budget by six percent in 2011 while cutting social programs.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Backed the Nation-State Law to anchor Israel's Jewish national character in Basic Law.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Describes African migration as a threat; his 2012 law detained unauthorized entrants; argues immigration controls help prevent terrorism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called the UN a "contemptuous farce" in 2024 and cited its condemnations of Israel as biased.

free-trade.rationale: Stated a simple rule: remove barriers to trade whenever possible, because money, trade and investment flow to freer economies and competition lowers costs (book, 'First Reforms').

nation-first.rationale: Pledged Israel will stand alone if necessary and wants to end dependence on US military aid.

open-borders.rationale: Backs tight immigration controls and urged central European states to close borders to illegal immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Treats economic growth as the engine of social progress and overrode environmental objections to gas extraction (book, 'This Is Social Justice!', 'Rising Power').

tech-solves-problems.rationale: 2024 UN speech proposes cooperation on AI, energy, water and agriculture as paths to prosperity.

central-planning.rationale: Repeatedly blames Israel's state-controlled, semi-socialist economy for stagnation and credits market reform for growth (book, 'First Reforms').

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Eliminated customs and sales taxes and states a rule of removing barriers to trade whenever possible (book, 'First Reforms' and 'Fat Man, Thin Man').

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mixed: favours market competition, but as prime minister personally pushed state backing for cyber, gas and science graduates and said only government intervention could expand engineering education (book, 'First Reforms', 'Rising Power').

democracy-best.rationale: Presents Israel as a democracy and asks nations to stand with democracy; no statement on voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Demanded a Likud party referendum on the Gaza disengagement and later backed direct election of the prime minister (book, 'A Clash of Head and Heart').

political-violence-never.rationale: Authorized a 1997 attempt to assassinate Hamas leader Khaled Mashal and praised the 2020 strike on Soleimani; this is state action, not revolution.

military-superiority.rationale: Raised the defense budget, authorized strikes on Iran and says Israel will defend itself regardless of outside support.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Calls Israel the nation-state of the Jewish people alone while promising equal rights to non-Jews; whether Jewish peoplehood counts as ethnic is contested.

taxation-theft.rationale: Treats taxing the able-bodied 'modestly' to help those who cannot work as legitimate; argues for low rather than no taxes (book, 'This Is Social Justice!').

conscription.rationale: His government defends military service and pushed a bill to integrate Haredim into the IDF, calling conscription targets a goal.

media-academia-power.rationale: Says a left-leaning media monopoly acted as his main opposition party, and that press, legal establishment and academia made common cause against decisions of voters (book, 'Politics 1988-1993', 'A Clash of Head and Heart').

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Bar-Ilan speech: Israel is the homeland of the Jewish people and the nation-state of the Jewish people.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Treats Israel as the homeland of the whole Jewish people, whose identity was forged there.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Froze government spending for three years and capped the budget deficit at 1% as finance minister.

national-self-determination.rationale: Insists on Jewish self-determination (Nation-State Law); accepted a conditional demilitarized Palestinian state in 2009 but opposes one imposed in 2024.

force-without-un.rationale: Authorized strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026 without UN Security Council approval and said Israel will act alone if needed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: His 2003-05 welfare-to-work program tied benefits to employment.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Personally pushed through legislation to develop offshore natural gas, overcame environmental objections, and made Israel an energy exporter (book, 'Rising Power').

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cut the state's size and taxes, but funds welfare for those who cannot work, infrastructure and state-led cyber and education programmes, so rejects a government limited to defence and justice (book, 'This Is Social Justice!', 'Rising Power').

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says the Jewish nation-state includes non-Jews with equal individual rights, though the Nation-State Law is criticized as unequal.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Presents Israel as the restored homeland of an indigenous people, not a colonial project.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Wrote that Israel should put its security first and 'when necessary strike first' (book, 'The Yom Kippur War'); ordered strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026 framed as preventive.

separated-powers.rationale: Said democracy is supposed to be checks and balances among the three branches and framed his judicial changes as restoring balance, though critics say they weaken the courts and the record is disputed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Finance Ministry under him threatened legislation limiting public-sector strike rights during the 2003 strikes.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mixed: says Israeli media is a left-leaning monopoly he wants opened to competition (book), but his government moved to close Al Jazeera's local bureau and advanced broadcasting changes.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Describes the US alliance as above politics, though he has said he wants to wean Israel off military aid.

death-penalty.rationale: Called for the death penalty for a 2017 attacker, backed the 2018 preliminary bill, and voted for the March 2026 law allowing hanging for convicted Palestinian terrorists.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Most recent position: opposes a Palestinian state since 2023 and led the 2024 Knesset vote against recognising one; earlier he accepted a conditional state (2009) and a Green Line-based framework (2014), and he opposed Oslo and the Gaza pullout.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Rejects the label of occupation for East Jerusalem's Jewish Quarter and the Western Wall, welcomed US recognition of Israeli sovereignty over the Golan, and denies Jews are occupiers in Judea and Samaria (book, 'Parting Shot', 'New Deal').

refugee-return.rationale: Bar-Ilan: the Palestinian refugee problem must be resolved outside Israel's borders.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Presents Zionism as the answer to the powerlessness of Jews in exile and Diaspora, and says Israel's economy should keep talent at home (book, 'Nobody Likes Goliath', 'First Reforms').

ban-cartels.rationale: As finance minister pushed laws against monopolies and cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: Describes his 2008-09 policy as not bailing out failed companies while other Western governments spent trillions (book, 'Firefighters').

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He framed the 2023 overhaul as restoring balance between elected officials and courts, citing millions of voters; he says he wants balance, not no limits.

single-official-language.rationale: Backed a Basic Law making Hebrew the state language with Arabic only a special status.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Backed the 2015-16 law requiring foreign-funded NGOs to disclose their sources; a disclosure rule rather than a ban.

non-intervention.rationale: Authorized strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026 described as aiming for regime change.

majority-settlement.rationale: Backed the Basic Law calling development of Jewish settlement a national value; expanded West Bank settlements.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Grounds Israel's claim in the Jewish people's ancient ties to the land: "this is the homeland of the Jewish people".

holocaust-denial.rationale: Treats the Holocaust as historical fact, comparing Hamas's 7 October attack to Nazi atrocities.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Says he supports equal rights for LGBT people and praises Israel as open on the issue.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Raised defense spending and calls Israel's military essential to survival.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Authorized pre-emptive strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026, framed as preventing existential threats.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Attacked the ICC prosecutor's moves against him and his defense minister as a rush to judgment; a rejection of this court's reach over Israel rather than the principle.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Speaks of the land as where Jewish identity was forged and commits to defending it.

notes:
Fresh audit replacing the 2026-10-14 one. Dropped old answers lacking an opened source (experts-over-public, rehabilitation, free-trade, tax-wealthy kept at -2 on record). Palestinian-state stance moved from a conditional 2009 acceptance to opposition by 2024; the more recent position is used. Israel's nuclear ambiguity policy means no answer on nuclear-weapon statements.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 19 answers taken from it, 28 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Main primary source is the 2022 memoir Bibi: My Story, read in full text and searched theme by theme; its self-praise for economic outcomes is treated as his claim, not established fact. Later positions come from speeches and reporting (2023 judicial overhaul and the Gaza war to 2026). On the courts he said in 2023 that a simple-majority override was a mistake while his government kept advancing other judicial changes, so those answers are mixed. His Palestinian-state position changed from the 2009 Bar-Ilan offer of a demilitarized state to flat rejection in 2025; the 2025 position wins. Same-sex marriage, abortion, religion-state questions and climate were not found in his own words and are null.
